items.q: Which brain systems share every goal?
items.a: One circuit does two jobs: **value assessment** and **action selection**. Key nodes: **amygdala** (avoidance/fear value), **basal ganglia** (go/no-go), **lateral PFC** (planning across time), **orbitofrontal cortex** (emotional progress vs future state). **Dopamine** is the common currency.

items.q: What's the difference between peripersonal and extrapersonal modes?
items.a: **Peripersonal** = consummatory here-and-now; progress *feeling* lives there. **Extrapersonal** = goal-directed beyond reach — you must **shift attention outward** to pursue, not only feel about the goal.

items.q: How does a 30–60 second visual lock help goal pursuit?
items.a: Narrow focus on a point **beyond reach** before acting recruits adrenaline and readiness. Emily Balcetis: eyes fixed on the goal line → **17% less perceived effort**, **23% faster**.

items.q: Should you visualize success or failure?
items.a: Routinely foreshadow **specific negative consequences of inaction** — near-**doubling** in goal attainment vs success visualization. Use **positive visualization only at the start**; the amygdala is built into the circuit.

items.q: What difficulty level keeps people pursuing?
items.a: **Moderate goals** just outside current ability — *"maybe I can, maybe I can't"* — nearly **double ongoing pursuit** vs goals that are too easy or impossible.

items.q: How should you place rewards to avoid dopamine crashes?
items.a: Don't fixate only on the finish line. Use **milestones** and **reward prediction error**: unexpected wins spike dopamine; fully anticipated rewards **pre-release** then underwhelm; misses drop **below baseline**. Do **weekly goal assessments** to re-up motivation.

items.q: What daily drill trains long-range goal cognition?
items.a: **Space-time bridging**: **90 s–3 min** shifting attention **interoception → palm → room → horizon → panoramic → return**. Near/internal focus = fine time slices; distant/broad focus = coarser future framing — practice builds flexible milestone + long-goal control.

items.q: Why prefer behavioral tools before caffeine or L-tyrosine?
items.a: Practiced **visual-attention drills** engage **neuroplasticity** in motivation/focus circuits themselves — you get better at being motivated by training the system, not only by stimulants.
